title: TMR ladder: what the "insane mesh aspect ratio" actually is
status: diagnosis complete; aspect ratio cleared as a solution defect; a separate, real bump convergence defect quantified and left open

checkmesh_aspect_ratio_definition.formula_2d: aspectRatio = max_dir(sum|Sf|_dir) / min_dir(sum|Sf|_dir), taken ONLY over directions where geometricD[dir]==1
checkmesh_aspect_ratio_definition.formula_3d_extra: if nDims==3, additionally max'd with (1/6)*sum|Sf| / V^(2/3)
checkmesh_aspect_ratio_definition.consequence: on an empty-patched 2D mesh the span direction is EXCLUDED; the reported number is the pure in-plane cell stretching, NOT a one-cell-thick-span artifact
checkmesh_aspect_ratio_definition.refuted_hypothesis: the initial hypothesis that the huge numbers were an artifact of the unit spanwise thickness is WRONG and is recorded as refuted
checkmesh_aspect_ratio_definition.evidence: checkMesh prints 'Mesh has 2 geometric (non-empty/wedge) directions (1 1 0)' (flat plate, bump) and '(1 0 1)' (NACA); pyHyp meshes print '(1 1 1)', i.e. 3 directions

flat_plate.geometry: x -1/3..2, y 0..1, span z 0..1 one cell, frontAndBack empty
flat_plate.note: max-AR cell is ON the plate, in the first wall-normal cell near the trailing end
flat_plate.trend: monotonically DECREASING under refinement, 74041 -> 64887, converging to ~64500
flat_plate.verdict: healthy: aspect ratio improves under refinement and the solution agrees with CFL3D to +0.2931% on the matched grid

bump_in_channel.geometry: x -25..26.5 (bump wall only x 0..1.5), y 0..5, span z 0..1 one cell, frontAndBack empty
bump_in_channel.key_finding: the max-AR cells are NOT on the viscous wall; they sit on the upstream/downstream SYMMETRY-plane extensions 20-25 units from the bump, in undisturbed flow
bump_in_channel.trend: increasing but CONVERGING: deltas +56132, +25750, +12246 -- halving each step, asymptote ~2.24e6

max_ar_in_bump_wall_band_x_0_to_1.5.trend: IMPROVES under refinement, opposite to the global maximum

bump_in_channel.verdict: the global maximum is a far-field artifact in uniform flow; the physically meaningful wall band tops out at 4714 and gets BETTER with refinement (4714 -> 4416 -> 4274) while the global maximum gets worse -- the two numbers move in opposite directions, which is why only the global one looks alarming

nasa_tmr_reference_grids.what: NASA Langley TMR's OWN distributed NACA0012 C-grids, the grids CFL3D and FUN3D use to produce the reference results this ladder is graded against
nasa_tmr_reference_grids.pipeline: plot3dToFoam -noBlank; autoPatch 80 -overwrite; span patches set to empty; checkMesh -allGeometry
nasa_tmr_reference_grids.reproduction_check: the 113x33 and 225x65 values reproduce the already-recorded 20650841.43 and 26446226.94 EXACTLY (demo-output/website/tmr/runs/naca-a0-coarse/log.checkMesh, naca-a10-medium/log.checkMesh), confirming the pipeline is faithful
nasa_tmr_reference_grids.headline: aspect ratio WORSENS monotonically under refinement on NASA's OWN reference grids: 20.65M -> 26.45M -> 29.90M
nasa_tmr_reference_grids.verdict: NASA's reference-grade grids fail OpenFOAM's aspect-ratio check by 20-30 MILLION, entirely in the far field / wake cut; within 1 chord of the airfoil the coarse grid's max AR is 87.6

pyhyp_generator_finding_crosscheck.geometric_directions: 3 (1 1 1) -- these are one-cell-thick 3D meshes, NOT empty-patched 2D
pyhyp_generator_finding_crosscheck.formula_branch_differs: because nDims==3, the pyHyp numbers use the volume-based branch and include the span direction; they are NOT computed the same way as the 2D TMR numbers and are not directly comparable
reasons: different generator: pyHyp hyperbolic extrusion vs blockMesh (flat plate, bump) and NASA's own plot3d grids (NACA)
different location: blunt trailing edge vs far field / wake cut
different verdict: pyHyp meshes PASS checkMesh's aspect-ratio check ('OK'); every TMR mesh FAILS it
different domain: ~16 chords vs ~500 chords, which is the dominant reason the absolute numbers differ
pyhyp_generator_finding_crosscheck.shared_phenomenon: both show max AR growing under refinement -- but NASA's own reference grids do this too (20.65M -> 29.90M), so the behaviour is NORMAL for a wall-resolved family whose farfield extent is held fixed while wall spacing halves; it is not by itself evidence of a generator defect
pyhyp_generator_finding_crosscheck.generator_fix_blocked_because: pyHyp is not installed on this host (python3 -c 'import pyhyp' -> ModuleNotFoundError), so the epsE/epsI/volSmoothIter scaling ablation the finding proposes could not be run; and it is not load-bearing for the TMR ladder, whose meshes pyHyp does not build

bump_convergence_defect.relation_to_aspect_ratio: investigated as a candidate cause and REFUTED by direct experiment (see wake_refinement_experiment)
bump_convergence_defect.confirmed_from_logs: none of the three rungs prints 'SIMPLE solution converged'; all stop at their iteration cap (4000/6000/9000)

residual_localisation_bump_coarse_t4000.method: solverInfo function object, writeResidualFields yes, on a faithful local rebuild of bump-coarse
residual_localisation_bump_coarse_t4000.note: the three fields that MISS their target (Ux, k, omega) concentrate their residual in the high-AR near-wake band x 1.9-5.2; p, which MEETS its target, has its own maximum on ordinary cells of AR 19-51

extended_run.case: faithful local rebuild of bump-coarse, run to 30000 iterations
extended_run.conclusion: the register's proposed fix ('extend bump-fine's iteration budget') is measured to be non-viable

cd_drift.why_this_matters: the cd_tail_spread metric used to certify the ladder (5.3e-8 on this rung) is ~4000x smaller than the actual accumulated drift and therefore badly understates the convergence error; the published bump Cd values carry an un-quantified convergence error of at least this order, and the drift direction (downward) would WORSEN, not improve, the fine rung's already-negative -1.126% deviation vs CFL3D

wake_refinement_experiment.purpose: test whether the extreme near-wake aspect ratio CAUSES the bump's residual stall, rather than merely co-locating with it
wake_refinement_experiment.what_changed_and_why: ONE variable: the downstream block's streamwise cell count nx_down 12 -> 48, with the total expansion ratio recomputed (455.85 -> 100.58) so the FIRST downstream cell is byte-identical at 0.0234375. Nothing else touched: same wall spacing, same y-grading, same upstream block, same schemes, same relaxation. Chosen because the residual is concentrated in exactly this block.
wake_refinement_experiment.verdict: cutting near-wake aspect ratio by 4.4x did NOT accelerate convergence -- the variant is SLOWER at every matched iteration including 30000 (Ux 1.606e-06 vs 1.231e-06) -- and did NOT reduce the Cd drift (-0.207% vs -0.197%, essentially identical). The spatial coincidence between the stalled residual and the high-AR cells is therefore NOT evidence of causation: the residual lives there because that is where the wake is developing, not because the cells are stretched. Aspect ratio is cleared as the cause of BOTH the bump convergence stall and the Cd drift.
wake_refinement_experiment.separate_minor_finding: downstream streamwise resolution does have a small real effect on Cd, +0.065% at 30000 iterations -- about a third of the convergence drift, and a genuine (small) grid sensitivity of the bump ladder that is not currently accounted for
wake_refinement_experiment.cause_of_bump_stall: still unidentified -- left open, not guessed at

answers.what_is_the_aspect_ratio_problem: checkMesh's aspect-ratio check (advisory threshold 1000) fires on every TMR mesh in the ladder. The reported number is genuine in-plane cell stretching, not a spanwise artifact. It is the geometrically necessary price of holding y+<1 at the wall while the domain extends 25 units (bump) or 500 chords (NACA) away.
answers.which_cases: all of them, at very different magnitudes: flat plate 6.5e4, bump 2.2e6, NASA NACA grids 2-3e7
answers.does_it_degrade_solutions_or_only_metric: only metrics, in every case tested. Flat plate: converges cleanly in 482-2846 iterations and matches CFL3D to +0.29%. Bump/NACA: the worst cells sit in far-field or wake-cut regions the answer does not depend on. Where a real defect DID co-locate with high-AR cells (the bump residual stall), removing the aspect ratio by 4.4x failed to fix it.
answers.does_it_worsen_under_refinement: depends on the family, and it is normal either way. Flat plate improves (74041->64887). Bump converges to an asymptote (2.14e6->2.23e6). NASA's own reference grids worsen (20.65M->29.90M). Since the gold-standard grids worsen, 'worsens under refinement' cannot by itself indicate a defect.
answers.is_it_the_pyhyp_generator_finding: No. Different generator, different formula branch, different magnitude, different location, and opposite checkMesh verdict (pass vs fail).
answers.does_it_explain_the_gradient_defect: No new evidence for a link. The existing null result (PROOF.md 19.2) stands, and this session adds an independent reason to doubt the link: the refinement-worsening signature is exhibited by NASA's own reference grids, so it is not anomalous enough to discriminate anything.
answers.did_the_ladder_advance: No new rung was solved. Bump-in-channel was already measured on three rungs before this session; what this session found is that those three rungs are NOT converged and carry a measured -0.197% drift, which is a repair job, not a new rung. Two new flat-plate mesh rungs (52224, 208896 cells) and one new NASA grid conversion (449x129) were measured for mesh metrics only, no solve.

open_items: the bump-in-channel convergence stall: real, quantified (-0.197% Cd drift, residuals 200-400x over target, not budget-limited), cause unidentified, aspect ratio ruled out

the published bump Cd numbers in demo-output/website/tmr/bump_sst.json and the wall.json research card carry an un-quantified convergence error and should not be quoted as a clean 1.1% agreement until repaired
the pyHyp epsE/epsI/volSmoothIter scaling ablation proposed by the generator finding remains unrun (pyHyp not installed on this host)

followup_2026_07_31.what: NASA's own bump grids fetched and measured; the bump ladder recomputed at matched iteration counts; the drag split into pressure and viscous parts.
followup_2026_07_31.correction_to_section_4: section 4 claimed 'max aspect ratio in the millions, worsening under refinement, is a normal property of a wall-resolved grid family with a fixed farfield extent'. The two halves separate. (a) WORSENING UNDER REFINEMENT IS normal and NASA's bump grids confirm it a third time, 4844.5 -> 5210.2, up 7.6%; the section-4 finding that mattered for the pyHyp question is untouched. (b) IN THE MILLIONS DOES NOT TRANSFER from the NACA0012 C-grid to the bump. The C-grid earns 20-30 million honestly, worst cells 271-476 chords out in a wake cut running to 569 chords. The bump has no wake cut and a 25-unit-each-way domain, and NASA's own bump grid at our exact node count has zero cells above 1e5 where ours has 68. The roadmap note's instinct that the bump number is abnormal is right; section 4 was wrong to wave it through as a family property.
followup_2026_07_31.aspect_ratio_verdict: not pathological as a solution defect and not the cause of the bump result, but a real defect of our generator rather than a family property. Inside the viscous wall band our grid (4714/4416/4274, improving under refinement) matches NASA's own (4844/5210). The 2.1e6 lives in uniform undisturbed flow 20-25 units from any wall, and section 7 already showed cutting it 4.4x changes neither convergence nor drift.
followup_2026_07_31.measurement_method: 4G_runs/structured_grid_aspect_ratio.py, checkMesh's own 2D branch computed from node coordinates, validated against checkMesh on NASA's NACA0012 113x33: 20650841.436 vs the recorded 20650841.43, ratio 1.000000. Our own three bump meshes were regenerated and reproduce 2136801.242 / 2192932.91 / 2218683.129 exactly.
followup_2026_07_31.iterative_error_verdict: does NOT swamp the discretization increments past n ~ 3000: p is stable at 0.511-0.519 across n = 3000..9000 matched. Below n = 3000 the ladder is worthless (p negative; at n = 2000 the increments cross and GCI reads -1545%). The published 0.5446 / 3.839% come from UNMATCHED caps 4000/6000/9000; matched at the same fine cap of 9000 the ladder reads p = 0.516, GCI 4.26%.
followup_2026_07_31.power_law_extrapolation_is_not_identifia: fitting Cd(n) = Cd_inf + A n^-q to the coarse trajectory over [1000,4000] predicts Cd(30000) to +0.027% but Cd_inf 1.9% low. The trajectory extrapolates; the limit does not.
followup_2026_07_31.why_p_is_0p52: a mixture artifact. Our viscous drag converges monotonically at p = 1.091; our pressure drag is NON-MONOTONE (increments -2.00e-05 then +6.42e-06) and has no observed order. CFL3D's pressure drag on the same grids converges at p = 2.914 from 3.7x our coarse-grid value. Compounding it, the family is not geometrically similar: our first wall cell scales x0.5337 then x0.5167 while every spacing in NASA's point-dropped family halves exactly, so there is no single h.

uq_gate.detail: Richardson lands 0.887 of the ladder's whole measured range beyond its finest rung against a 0.15 tolerance; fires on the published and the matched ladder alike.
uq_gate.incidental_finding: read from source, not inferred: ladder_band (uq.py:93) and eca_hoekstra_band (uq.py:287) both hard-code h = (1/N)**(1/3), the 3D convention. On a 2D case, where doubling both directions quadruples N, r21 becomes 4**(1/3) = 1.587 instead of the true 2, so the reported observed order is 0.817 where the 2D calculation gives 0.545. Verdict unchanged here (both routes return conclusive False), but the order printed on any 2D ladder is overstated by that factor -- a 2D ladder whose true order was 1.6 would print 2.4 and fall outside the credible range for the wrong reason. Flagged, not edited; sdk/chief_engineer/ is out of scope for this session.

followup_2026_07_31.next_step_now_concrete: rebuild the bump family from NASA's own distributed grids (two of three now held at models/tmr/bump/grids/), as the NACA0012 case was already pivoted on 2026-07-26. One h, clustering where the physics is, and a pressure drag that converges at p = 2.91 in CFL3D's hands on those very grids.

fine.termination: the re-run stopped at iteration 10098 of a requested 15000; its log ends mid-iteration with no error, no OOM in dmesg and 407 GB free. Cause not identified. 10098 is past the published 9000 cap, which is what the matched table needed, so it was not re-run.

iterative_drift_per_rung.reading: the drift is near common-mode across rungs, which is why it largely cancels out of the increments and the matched observed order is stable past n~3000. The ladder's ORDER survives the iterative error; its VALUES do not -- every Cd on it is low-biased by roughly 0.2% and still falling, in the direction that widens the gap to CFL3D rather than closing it.

matched_window_9000_to_10000_pct.reading: all three descend within 27% of each other over one identical window, fine fastest and coarse slowest. The cancellation is good but not exact, and the residue biases the observed order slightly downward as the ladder runs: p goes 0.5191 at n=6000 to 0.5140 at n=10000, decelerating.

our_bump_grids_remeasured_this_session.reproduction: global maxima and wall-band maxima both reproduce the 2026-07-30 values exactly (2136801.242 / 2192932.91; 4714.0 / 4416.0)
our_bump_grids_remeasured_this_session.discriminator: checkMesh's default 1000 threshold flags hundreds of cells on BOTH families and discriminates nothing. AR > 1e5 separates them completely: 68 and 260 cells for ours against 0 and 0 for NASA's.

drag_decomposition_at_matched_iterations.why: the 10.4 claim must not rest on the same unequal caps 10.3 convicts the published total of. forceCoeffs prints the Total/Pressure/Viscous split every iteration into log.simpleFoam, so it is recoverable at matched counts for free.
drag_decomposition_at_matched_iterations.verdict: the pressure sign flip holds at EVERY matched count tested, and the second increment grows steadily MORE positive as the rungs converge rather than shrinking toward zero. The pressure drag is not a nearly-converged quantity a longer run would tidy up; it is going the wrong way and going there harder. The viscous order is stable at 1.03-1.07 matched against 1.090 published.
